sermon.title: Adding Brotherly Love
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: The speaker defines brotherly love as loving the true church and says it confirms new birth (1 Peter 1:22–23). God and the apostles teach it (1 Thessalonians 4; John 13:34); loving the brethren is serving Jesus because the church is his body (Acts 9:4; Matthew 25:40). He warns that not discerning the Lord’s body brings sickness and death (1 Corinthians 11:29), describes the church as a place of healing, word, repentance, and good works, and urges assembling to stir up love (Hebrews 10:24–26).
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Caption corrections include “2 Peter” for “ii Peter,” “Revelation” for “revelations,” “Mary sat” for “mary said,” and verse colon formatting. Sensitive: he says he has seen people die early, become sickly, or mentally depressed for attacking the church; warns Christian humanists; links willful sin against a brother to no remaining sacrifice (Hebrews 10). Speaker not named in recording; series continuity—confirm Pastor David G. Kincer.

chunks.section_question: What is the Bible definition of brotherly love?
chunks.short_answer: He says brotherly love is to love the true church, its membership, the true believer, and that it is confirmation of being born again—a change from wrong behavior and thinking to right by the Scriptures. He reads 1 Peter 1:22–23 about purifying souls in obeying the truth unto genuine brotherly love, loving one another fervently with a pure heart.
chunks.text: We’re again going to 2 Peter chapter 1 verses 4 through 5, and we’re going to be talking about adding brotherly love to godliness, self-control, knowledge, virtue, and faith. The Bible definition of brotherly love is to love the true church, the true church’s membership, the true believer. Brotherly love is confirmation of being born again—is going to be our first look at brotherly love. It’s a confirmation of being born again. Born again is a change from wrong behavior and thinking to a right behavior and thinking by the Scriptures. In 1 Peter chapter 1 verse 22 and 23, you have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto a genuine brotherly love. See that you love one another with a pure heart fervently—enthusiastically. See that you love one another with enthusiasm. Being born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, by the word of God.

chunks.section_question: Is brotherly love confirmation that you have been born again?
chunks.short_answer: He says most people know John 3 about being born of the Spirit, but Jesus also said his word is spirit—so both the Spirit and the word change our lives. Brotherly love confirms you have really been born again, and it is taught by God himself and his apostles.
chunks.text: Most people understand that in John chapter 3 we are born again by the Spirit, but you also got to understand in John Jesus said my word is spirit. And not only does the Spirit come and personally change our lives, but the word of God comes and changes our life and moves us to apply the things of God in our life. So brotherly love is the confirmation that you’ve really been born again. Brotherly love is taught by God himself and his apostles.

chunks.section_question: What did God and Jesus teach about loving one another?
chunks.short_answer: He reads 1 Thessalonians 4:9 that you are taught by God to love one another, and John 13:34 to love one another as Jesus loved you. By this all will know you are his disciples. He contrasts teachers who will not consent to Jesus’ wholesome words (1 Timothy 6:3).
chunks.text: In 1 Thessalonians 4:9 through 12, concerning brotherly love, you have no need that I write unto you, as you are taught by God to love one another. God has taught you personally by Spirit when you got born again to love one another, and you do to all the brethren in Macedonia. You do that. But in 1 Timothy 6:3, if any man teach and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ—okay, what did Jesus teach? John 13:34, love one another as I have loved you. Tells us how to love one another as he loved us. By this shall all men know you’re my disciples. He says there is an end result of loving one another, loving the true church, and is that other people outside will know that you are my disciplined ones, my pupils, my disciples.

chunks.short_answer: He cites John 16:13 that the Spirit guides into all truth, and says the apostles urge believers to increase more and more—not only love brethren in Macedonia or the same culture and nationality, but love the brethren worldwide, state to state and nation to nation. They also seek a quiet life, working with your own hands, paying your own bills.
chunks.text: John 16:13, the Spirit of truth will guide you into all truth. So the Spirit comes and teaches us, Jesus comes and teaches us, God comes and teaches us himself to love the church of the living God. He goes on to say in 1 Thessalonians 4:9, we urge you—now it’s the apostles talking—we the apostles urge you, brethren, to increase more and more. Don’t just love the brethren in Macedonia. Just don’t love people in your same culture, your same nationality, whatever, but increase more and more. Go on to the next state. Go on to the next nation. Love the brethren worldwide. Increase more and more. And he says we also aspire you—we seek that you lead a quiet life. You’re not a lawless people doing violence and killing people and robbing—a quiet life—and take care of your own affairs, working with your own hands. Drive your own self to work. Don’t expect other Christians to do things for you. Pay your own bills. Balance your own checkbook. Get your act together and work, as we commanded you.

chunks.text: We’re going to go to Romans chapter 12 verse 10 through 13. Be kindly affectionate one to another with brotherly love. And then he tells us how to do it: in honor giving preference—they’re number one. You make your brother number one. Not lagging in diligence—working hard at making your brother number one and loving your brother. Fervent in spirit in loving your brother and making them number one. Serving the Lord. Distributing to the needs of the saints and given to hospitality. Invite people to your house to put them first and to encourage them in the things of God.

chunks.section_question: How is loving your brother serving the Lord Jesus?
chunks.short_answer: He reads Acts 9:4—Jesus told Saul, why are you persecuting me?—though Saul was persecuting the church. Messing with the church is messing with Jesus. The church is Christ’s body (1 Corinthians 12:27; Colossians 1:24); Matthew 25:40 says as you did it to the least of these my brethren you did it to me.
chunks.text: Now we’re going to focus in on this serving the Lord. How is that serving the Lord when I love my brother? How am I ministering to Jesus when I’m loving my brother, making them number one? And so we’re going to ask this question: How is brotherly love serving the Lord Jesus Christ? And we’re going to go to Acts chapter 9 verse 4. When Saul saw the light, Jesus appeared to Saul on the road, and he said to Saul, why are you persecuting me? And Saul says, well who are you? And Jesus replied, I am Jesus whom you are persecuting. Now Paul was not persecuting Jesus—Jesus was in heaven—but he was persecuting the church, and Jesus is plainly saying when you mess with the church you’re messing with me. And we find in 1 Corinthians 12:27 that we are the body of Christ. Colossians 1:24, Christ for the sake of his body, which is the church. The church is the body of Christ. And Matthew 25:40, as you did it to the least of these my brethren you did it unto me. You see, we are the body of Christ—the eyes, the mouth, the hands, the feet of Christ on the earth—and how we treat our fellow Christian believer, our true believer brother in Christ, is how we’re treating God.

chunks.section_question: What does 1 Corinthians 11 say happens if you mistreat the Lord’s body?
chunks.short_answer: He reads that not discerning the Lord’s body—his church—causes many to be sick and weak, and many have died, for purposely mistreating God’s people. He warns Christian humanists to be careful how they speak evil of the true church; he says he has seen people die early or become sickly and depressed for attacking the church.
chunks.text: Now knowing that, you’ve got to understand in 1 Corinthians 11 that it is taken seriously about our attitude toward the real body of Christ, toward the real church, the real believers. And he says in 1 Corinthians 11:29, you’re not discerning the Lord’s body, which is what—his church, which is Jesus. For this cause many are sick and weakly among you, and many have already died, because you have mistreated purposely the body of Christ, the people of God. So I say to Christian humanists, be careful how you treat and how you speak evil and attack the true church, because Jesus will correct you. And folks, I have seen people die early for attacking the church. I have seen people sickly and mentally depressed and cast down. God does back up his word. When you purposely, on purpose, attack God’s people, Jesus will deal with that.

chunks.section_question: What needs of the saints should the church meet?
chunks.short_answer: Besides food, clothing, shelter, and medicine, he lists healing of mind, emotions, spirit, and body (Luke 9:11); hearing the word, not opinions or psychology (Luke 10:39–42); a place to repent (Luke 15:7); and maintaining good works and job skills so you are not unfruitful (Titus 3:14).
chunks.text: Now the deeds of the saints—you see, that’s how we serve the Lord, by serving his people. Now the needs of the saints—what might the needs of the saints be besides food, clothing, shelter, and medicine? Okay. In Luke 9:11, they came to him and Jesus healed all them that had need of healing. There are people who need healing in their mind and their emotions, in their spirit and in their physical body. So the church is to be a place of healing. In Luke 10:39, Mary sat at Jesus’s feet hearing his word, and Jesus said one thing is needful, and Mary chose that good part. The church should have the word of God spoken in it—not opinions and psychology and philosophies, but the word of God, the living word of God. Luke 15:7, more joy over one that repents than 99 just persons who need no repentance. So the church should be a place where people can repent, change their thinking and change their ways. Titus 3:14, learn to maintain good works to meet the necessary needs so you will not be unfruitful, both natural and spiritual. If you get an education, get a job skill, and work hard and be honest, you will provide for yourself. If you seek God he will give you the true riches of his kingdom.

chunks.section_question: What if a church says it is rich and needs nothing?
chunks.short_answer: He reads Revelation 3:17—miserable, poor, blind, and naked spiritually—and 2 Peter that lacking these added qualities makes you blind. The church should build self-control (1 Corinthians 7:5) and perfect what is lacking in faith (1 Thessalonians 3:10)—virtue, knowledge, self-control, godliness, patience, and brotherly love.
chunks.text: In Revelation chapter 3 verse 17, you say I am rich—this is to the church; he’s talking to believers—I have need of nothing, and you don’t know that you’re miserable, poor, blind, and naked. You’re in pain. You’re poor spiritually. You’re blind spiritually. And you are naked—you don’t have the clothes of righteousness. And remember in 2 Peter, he that lacks these things is blind and can’t see afar off. When we don’t add to our faith we become blind. 1 Corinthians 7:5, so Satan does not tempt you because of your lack of self-control. A church should be a place where people can build up their strength in controlling themselves. 1 Thessalonians 3:10, we might perfect that which is lacking in your faith. You see, we need to add virtue, knowledge, self-control, godliness, patience, and brotherly love.

chunks.section_question: What should church services be for, according to Hebrews 10?
chunks.short_answer: He says not entertaining and socializing, but provoking one another to love and good works, not forsaking assembling, coming to give and stir up, exhorting one another all the more as the day approaches. The purpose is to build people from babyhood to fatherhood in Christ.
chunks.text: Now the urgency of church services to meet the needs of the saints is very important. Hebrews 10:24, we shouldn’t be here for entertaining and socializing. We should be here for the purpose that the church is—provoke, stir up one another to love and to good works. That’s what a church service should be about. And how do we do it? Not forsaking the assembling of yourselves together, as some are, and not coming to get all the time but come to give, to stir up. He says exhort one another, encourage one another in love and good works, and so much the more as you see the day approaching. The purpose of the church is to keep building the people up from babyhood to childhood to young adulthood to fatherhood in Christ. It’s urgent and it’s important that we do that.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about willfully hurting a brother after knowing the truth?
chunks.short_answer: He reads that if we sin willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth there remains no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful expectation of judgment. He says purposely hurting or speaking to hurt a brother falls under that, and that we must apply brotherly love at every growth stage; God will deal with those who do not love his church.
chunks.text: He goes on to say if we sin willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth there remains no more sacrifice for sins. If I purposely and intentionally do something to hurt you or speak of you to hurt you, God said there’s no more sacrifice for your sin, but a fearful looking of judgment and fiery indignation which shall devour the adversaries. I submit to you today that we need to apply brotherly love to our faith and love our brother who is a genuine follower of Christ, whether they are a baby, child stage, young adult stage, or the mature stage. God will deal with people that do not love his church. You.

faqs.question: What qualities does he say brotherly love is added to?
faqs.answer: He says they are adding brotherly love to godliness, self-control, knowledge, virtue, and faith from 2 Peter 1.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.

faqs.question: Are we born again only by the Spirit, or also by the word?
faqs.answer: He says John 3 teaches birth by the Spirit, but Jesus also said his word is spirit—so the word of God also changes our life and moves us to apply the things of God.

faqs.question: How will all men know you are Jesus’ disciples?
faqs.answer: He reads John 13:34–35: love one another as I have loved you; by this all men will know you are my disciples.

scriptures.text_nkjv: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another.”

faqs.question: What does “lead a quiet life” and work with your own hands mean here?
faqs.answer: He says you are not lawless—doing violence, killing, or robbing—but take care of your own affairs, work with your hands, pay your bills, balance your checkbook, and do not expect other Christians to do everything for you.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But concerning brotherly love you have no need that I should write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another; and indeed you do so toward all the brethren who are in all Macedonia. But we urge you, brethren, that you increase more and more; that you also aspire to lead a quiet life, to mind your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you, that you may walk properly toward those who are outside, and that you may lack nothing.

faqs.question: Why did Jesus ask Saul why he was persecuting him?
faqs.answer: He says Saul was persecuting the church, not Jesus in heaven, but Jesus said when you mess with the church you are messing with me.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then he fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?” And he said, “Who are You, Lord?” Then the Lord said, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. It is hard for you to kick against the goads.”

faqs.question: What does Matthew 25:40 mean for treating fellow believers?
faqs.answer: He says as you did it to the least of these my brethren you did it unto me—how we treat a true believer brother is how we are treating God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the King will answer and say to them, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me.’

faqs.question: What warning does he give Christian humanists about the true church?
faqs.answer: He says be careful how you treat, speak evil of, and attack the true church, because Jesus will correct you and backs up his word when you purposely attack God’s people.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body. For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep.

faqs.question: What “one thing is needful” does he apply to the church from Mary?
faqs.answer: He says Mary sat at Jesus’ feet hearing his word and chose the good part—so the church should speak the living word of God, not opinions, psychology, and philosophies.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard His word. But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she approached Him and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Therefore tell her to help me.” And Jesus answered and said to her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about many things. But one thing is needed, and Mary has chosen that good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

faqs.question: What does Revelation 3:17 say to a self-satisfied church?
faqs.answer: He says believers who claim to be rich and need nothing do not know they are miserable, poor, blind, and naked—without the clothes of righteousness.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Because you say, ‘I am rich, have become wealthy, and have need of nothing’—and do not know that you are wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked—

faqs.question: Should you come to church mainly to get or to give?
faqs.answer: He says not forsaking assembling, and not coming to get all the time but come to give, to stir up—exhort and encourage one another in love and good works.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

faqs.question: At what growth stages should you love a genuine follower of Christ?
faqs.answer: He says love your brother whether they are a baby, child stage, young adult stage, or the mature stage; God will deal with people who do not love his church.
